title: What a Five-Page Business Website Should Include

cover.alt: Concept illustration of five connected portfolio panels representing the core pages of a business website.

figures.title: One clear job for each page
figures.summary: A compact site works when every page answers a different need.

items.label: Home
items.detail: Explain the offer and route visitors to useful detail.

items.label: About
items.detail: Introduce the people, relevant experience, and service area.

items.label: Services
items.detail: Describe specific work, inclusions, pricing context, and next steps.

items.label: Proof
items.detail: Show genuine testimonials or documented project examples.

figures.caption: The five-page structure described in the article; page count alone does not establish effectiveness.

figures.title: Connect information to a useful action
figures.summary: Page links should help someone move from interest to a conversation.

items.label: Find the relevant service
items.detail: Link Home summaries to detailed service information.

items.label: Check the people and work
items.detail: Connect About to genuine testimonials or case studies.

items.label: Resolve the practical questions
items.detail: Make service scope, pricing context, and coverage easy to find.

items.label: Make contact
items.detail: Give service and proof pages a clear route to the Contact page.

figures.caption: A suggested reading path from the article. Visitors can enter at any page, so each page needs context.
